title: Per-tenant optimizer: rule evaluator, safe apply, and rollback orchestrator
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Customers exhibit very different latency and quality tolerances. Manual tuning of batching and KV/prefix caching per route is labor-intensive and error-prone. We need an automated per-tenant optimizer that recommends and safely applies batching/caching configs (and can roll them back) based on segmentation rules, allowlists/denylists, and tiered entitlements.

Goal: Build a rule-evaluation engine and reconcile/apply orchestration that: 1) computes per-tenant and per-route recommendations for batching and cache settings, 2) validates recommendations against safety policies (allowlist/denylist, SLA tiers), 3) runs staged dry-runs and canaries, 4) applies changes with monitoring and automatic rollback when regressions are detected.

Scope: MVP covers supported hosted and dedicated routes (text generation and chat). Private deployments will be supported via an agent in a follow-up. This ticket focuses on the engine, rollout orchestration, and observability integrations needed to operate safe automated applies.
acceptance_criteria: Rule evaluator produces deterministic recommendation JSON for a tenant+route given telemetry input and segmentation profile
Safety policy checks reject any recommendation that would reduce a route below its SLA latency or change model family without explicit whitelisting
Dry-run subsystem simulates cost/latency impact and stores expected delta in a dashboard
Canary rollout applies to 1% of traffic for a tenant and triggers rollback if quality or latency thresholds breach within 30 minutes
Automated rollback reverses config and emits incident with root-cause hints when thresholds are breached
End-to-end e2e tests and a runbook exist and are linked in the ticket
design_notes: Segmentation: tenants assigned to segments (free/prod/enterprise) via existing billing/entitlement service; segments drive max allowed aggressiveness in batching and whether model-variant downgrade is permitted
Evaluator inputs: recent 1h and 24h histograms of seq length, tokens/request, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, and token cost; static tenant preferences from metadata
Recommendation space: batch size target, max concurrent tokens, prefix cache TTL, KV cache warm thresholds, quantization variant suggestion (qualitative)

Safety gates: allowlist (explicit tenants allowed to downgrade model family), denylist (tenants that cannot be auto-tuned), SLA check (p95 latency floor), quality check (synthetic prompt evals baseline), and manual approval flag for enterprise tier

Architecture: stateless rule evaluator service (k8s) + reconciliation worker that posts diffs to config-store (etcd) behind a feature-flagged apply controller; apply controller coordinates dry-run, canary, and full rollout
Simulation: use request-replay from a sampled trace to estimate latency/cost delta for a proposed change rather than blind heuristics
Rollback triggers: latency increase >10% p95 or quality regression >3% on eval set, error rate spike >50% absolute or secondary system alert
Telemetry: extend Console dashboards to show expected vs actual cost deltas, canary cohort latency, and last successful config per-tenant
rollout_plan: Week 1: implement evaluator and basic recommendation schema; unit tests for deterministic outputs
Week 2: safety policy engine + simulation harness using historical traces; PR review
Week 3: reconciliation worker + dry-run flow; integrate with console dashboard (read-only) for PM/SE review
Week 4: canary apply controller with 1% traffic cohorts; limited internal tenants only
Week 5: extended canary across selected low-risk customers and monitor for two weeks
Week 6: enable auto-rollback and expand to broader tenant cohorts after sign-off
metrics: false_positive rate for rollback triggers (manual overrides)
dependencies: ENG-34108 (policy-orchestrator) - for reuse of policy evaluation primitives
Console dashboard API (observability team) - for widgets and alerts
comments: 2026-03-02 - Avery Chen: Triage complete. Recommend P1 due to recurring manual effort and cost leakage on large tenants.
2026-03-04 - Rohit Malhotra: Spike finished. Evaluator returns stable recommendations given the sampled 24h trace. Noted edge case where very bursty tenants cause poor dry-run estimates.
2026-03-05 - Lina Ortiz (SRE): Suggest adding an extra safety check to prevent simultaneous auto-applies across dependent routes for the same tenant to avoid cascading latency effects.
2026-03-07 - Rohit Malhotra: Implemented route-level mutex in reconciliation worker. Added a conservative default for bursty tenants to require manual approval.
2026-03-08 - PM Priya Singh: Product asks that enterprise tier never automatically downgrades model family; added to safety policy and sentinel test.
2026-03-09 - Rohit Malhotra: Canary start scheduled for 2026-03-11 on internal trials only. Added logging to surface synthetic-eval deltas alongside telemetry.

2026-03-10 - Engineering: Found a regression in simulation when seq length distribution changes abruptly; mitigation: use sliding-window weighted histograms and conservative headroom in initial rollout. Added to follow-up backlog.
